title: First-Line LLM Quality Triage & Eval Handoff Playbook
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook describes the first-line process for handling customer-reported LLM quality issues during enterprise onboarding and the formal handoff to Applied ML / eng teams for evaluation and remediation. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Support Tier 1/2, Solutions Engineers (SEs), and Applied ML reviewers.

Goals:
- Quickly triage user-facing quality regressions and determine severity.
- Capture reproducible test cases and metadata needed for deterministic evals.
- Execute lightweight mitigations (prompt guardrails, model switchover, reranking) when safe.
- Perform a clean handoff to Applied ML or Eng with a complete evaluation package.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated customers during the first 90 days of onboarding and to production incidents that are suspected regressions in model output quality.
- Not intended for purely infrastructure outages (see incident playbooks).

Owner and Roles:
- Customer Success (owner): overall coordination, communication with customer.
- Support Tier 1: initial intake, basic repro steps, short-term mitigations.
- Support Tier 2 / CSE: advanced triage, telemetry capture, auth to access customer logs.
- Solutions Eng: assist with integration-level fixes (payload / tokenization).
- Applied ML: run evaluations, propose model/strategy changes, approve rollouts.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: engineering fixes for runtime-related degradation (KV cache, batching issues).

Contact Channels:
- Slack channel: #cs-quality-triage (pager: @cs-oncall)
- Pager (for sev-2+ regressions): CS Ops Escalation Pager (see oncall rota)
- Email: cs-incident@redwood.ai (for formal handoffs)

Severity Matrix (Guidance)
- Sev 1 (Critical): Customer-facing data corruption, hallucinations causing safety/regulatory violations, or blocking revenue-generating flows. Response target: 1 hour.
- Sev 2 (High): Severe quality regression affecting major workflows but with an acceptable workaround. Response target: 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Localized quality issues or intermittent regressions. Response target: 24 hours.
- Sev 4 (Low): Cosmetic or non-urgent degradations. Response target: 3 business days.

Immediate Intake Checklist (Support Tier 1)
1. Record incident metadata in ticket system (CS-Ticket-Template): customer ID, environment (hosted/dedicated/private), model name + pinned version, route name, time window, example prompt(s), example outputs, user-visible impact, and severity estimate.
2. Confirm customer can reproduce and capture a minimal reproducible test case (MRT): short prompt, model config (max_tokens, temperature, top_p), and exact API request payload if possible.
3. Capture opaque IDs: request_id, trace_id, tenant_id, and model_instance_id (if present).
4. Check common quick mitigations: revert to previously pinned model variant, lower temperature to 0.2, enable deterministic sampling, or temporarily route to fallback model. Document actions.

Telemetry & Artifacts to Collect (Tier 2 / CSE)
- Request logs: full request/response bodies (redact PII per data-retention policy).
- Token-level latency histogram for the requests in question.
- Trace (X-Trace-ID) and corresponding route logs in the console.
- Model serving metrics: batch size, KV cache hit rate, gpu_util (%), model_load_error_count.
- Prompt/response diffs: before/after changes to prompts or system messages.
- Evaluation harness snapshot: failing test cases saved as a JSONL file with fields: "input","expected","actual","model","seed","config". Example: 

Example eval snapshot (JSONL line):
{"input":"Summarize the following policy: ...","expected":"Key points: A, B, C","actual":"Irrelevant personal opinion","model":"gpt-open-64b-v2","seed":1234,"config":"{\"temperature\":0.7,\"max_tokens\":256}"}

Lightweight Repro Steps (run locally / from console)
- Recommended curl example for reproducibility (hosted API):

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{REDACTED}}" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-64b-v2","input":"<INSERT_PROMPT>","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":200}'

- For streaming routes, include stream flag to capture chunk ordering.
- For embeddings regressions use /v1/embeddings and include the index id and vector fingerprint.

Quick Mitigations (to attempt before escalation)
- Prompt-level: tighten system messages, add positive/negative examples, or add explicit instructions to avoid forbidden content.
- Model switch: move to a verified-stable variant (documented in the model catalog) and monitor.
- Config change: reduce temperature, set top_p to 0.0, set max_tokens to stricter limit.
- Rate-limit adjustment: check for token-throttling-induced truncation.

When to Escalate to Applied ML / Eng
Escalate if any of the following are true:
- MRT reproduces a quality regression on the verified-stable model catalog variant.
- Problem appears after a model rollout or quantization change.
- There is evidence of runtime-level anomalies (batching misordering, cache poisoning, sequence length handling).
- Customer impact meets Sev 1/Sev 2 thresholds.

Required Handoff Payload (email and ticket body)
1. Executive summary (1-2 sentences): observed regression, impact, and customer business effect.
2. Severity and SLA target.
3. MRT JSONL file (attached) with at least 3 failing and 3 passing cases.
4. Telemetry links (console traces, request IDs, metric charts) with timestamps.
5. Exact model config used and recommended mitigation attempts and results.
6. Access notes (whether customer has consented to sharing PII and any additional privacy constraints).
7. Point of contact for customer + next check-in ETA.

Sample Handoff Email Subject:
[Handoff] Customer ACME Corp — Sev2 hallucination regression — model gpt-open-64b-v2 — 2026-02-15

Advanced Investigation Steps (Applied ML)
1. Re-run failing MRT against the model binaries used in production (note quantization/FP config). Record random seeds.
2. Run delta-eval: compare outputs across model variants and quantization profiles, and record semantic similarity metrics (BERTScore >= 0.92 expected for paraphrase-preservation).
3. Run targeted attribution tests if hallucination suspected (prompt perturbation and source retrieval trace).
4. If embedding degradation: compute recall@K and centroids shifts, and run index consistency checks (shard consistency, vector dimensionality).
5. If runtime suspected: validate KV cache lookup for long-context queries (KV cache hit rate should be > 98% for identical prefixes).
6. Produce remediation recommendation: prompt patch, model rollback, re-quantize, or runtime patch, plus monitoring gating criteria.

Rollout & Canary Guidance
- Any model or runtime fix must be rolled out as a canary to 1–5% of traffic for 24–72 hours with automated quality regression checks.
- Key metrics to monitor during canary: failure_rate, latency_p95, token_cost_per_request, semantic_similarity_score, customer-reported TTR.
- Automatic rollback trigger: >3x increase in failure_rate or >5 point drop in semantic_similarity_score over baseline.

Communication and Customer Updates
- For Sev1/Sev2 incidents provide hourly updates until mitigated.
- For Sev3 provide daily updates until resolved.
- Use templated status updates (see CS incident templates) and always include: what we know, what we tried, next steps, ETA.

Post-Incident Activities
- Postmortem owner: Applied ML if model-related; Eng-Serving-Runtime if runtime-related; CS owner for communications.
- Postmortem template fields: timeline, root cause hypothesis, evidence, mitigation, follow-ups, and action owner + due date.
- Create evergreen test cases in the eval-harness repo and add to the customer-specific prompt set for regression monitoring.

Operational Metrics & SLOs (for monitoring quality during onboarding)
- Quality baseline: semantic_similarity_score (customer prompt set) >= 0.88 for pass.
- False hallucination rate <= 1% for critical domains (legal, finance, regulated content).
- Regression detection latency: alert < 6 hours from first customer report or automated detection.

Templates and Artifacts (links)
- CS-Ticket-Template (use when creating an intake ticket)
- Eval harness snapshot template (JSONL)
- Onboarding prompt set location: /datasets/onboarding_prompts/{customer_id} (request access via SE)
- Model catalog: /tools/model-catalog (contains verified-stable variants)

Security and Data Privacy Notes
- Always follow the Sensitive Data Handling Policy when collecting request/response bodies. Redact or pseudonymize PII before sharing with applied/engineering teams unless explicit customer consent is recorded.
- For private and on-prem customers, ensure handoff procedures respect the customer's network and data-residency constraints — attachments should be stored in the customer's secure workspace.

Training & Playbook Refresh
- CSEs and Tier 2 are expected to run through the playbook in quarterly game-days.
- This playbook is reviewed every 6 months; file change requests should be submitted to the owner (Customer Success) with supporting examples.

Appendix: Quick check commands and grep helpers
- Find recent requests containing a prompt substring (console CLI):
redwood-cli logs query --tenant acme-corp --from 2026-02-10T00:00:00Z --to 2026-02-15T00:00:00Z --query "prompt:\"refund policy\""

- Extract request IDs that match a trace and dump bodies (example jq filter):
redwood-cli logs tail --trace 1234abcd | jq -r '. | select(.route=="/v1/generate") | {request_id: .id, payload: .body}'

- Basic JSONL eval harness format reminder:
input\texpected\tactual\tmodel\tseed\tconfig
Use tab-separated JSONL for import into evaluation tools.
